steps: Add resources.limits for memory and CPU to each container
Add resources.requests to enable proper scheduling
Consider LimitRange defaults at the namespace level

findings.name: Deployment containers omit resource requests
findings.message: Deployment containers omit resource requests; HPA and scheduler decisions will be unreliable

steps: Set resources.requests.cpu and resources.requests.memory on every container
Align requests with observed steady-state usage
Ensure requests are set when using HPA

next_step.description: Set resources.requests.cpu and resources.requests.memory on every container

findings.name: Container does not enforce readOnlyRootFilesystem
findings.message: Container metrics does not set readOnlyRootFilesystem: true

steps: Set securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem to true on every container
Use emptyDir or tmpfs mounts for directories that need write access

next_step.description: Set securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem to true on every container

findings.name: Deployment explicitly sets replicas to 1
findings.message: Deployment has replicas: 1; no high availability

steps: Set replicas to at least 2 for services requiring availability
Use HPA with minReplicas >= 2 for auto-scaling workloads
Single replica is acceptable for batch jobs or development

next_step.description: Set replicas to at least 2 for services requiring availability

findings.name: Deployment does not disable automountServiceAccountToken
findings.message: Deployment does not set automountServiceAccountToken: false; pods get unnecessary API credentials

steps: Set automountServiceAccountToken to false in the pod spec
Only enable it for pods that genuinely need Kubernetes API access
Use dedicated service accounts with minimal RBAC for pods that need API access

next_step.description: Set automountServiceAccountToken to false in the pod spec

findings.name: ClusterRole grants nodes/proxy enabling Kubelet API RCE
findings.message: ClusterRole grants nodes/proxy access, enabling full Kubelet API (exec/run/attach) on all nodes

steps: Audit all ClusterRoles for nodes/proxy permissions
Remove nodes/proxy from ClusterRole rules unless strictly required
Implement network policies restricting pod access to port 10250
Deploy node-level runtime detection (Falco, Tetragon) for Kubelet connections
Consider deploying Kyverno policy restrict-clusterrole-nodesproxy as admission guard
Kyverno equivalents: KPOL-0279 and KPOL-0367
Monitor KEP-2862 progress for fine-grained Kubelet authorization (K8s 1.36+)
commands: kubectl get clusterroles -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.rules[]?.resources[]? == "nodes/proxy") | .metadata.name'
kubectl get clusterrolebindings -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.roleRef.name == "<ROLE_NAME>") | {name: .metadata.name, subjects: .subjects}'

next_step.description: Audit all ClusterRoles for nodes/proxy permissions
next_step.command: kubectl get clusterroles -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.rules[]?.resources[]? == "nodes/proxy") | .metadata.name'

findings.name: ClusterRoleBinding binds nodes/proxy ClusterRole to subjects
findings.message: ClusterRoleBinding grants nodes/proxy via ClusterRole "k8s-ephemeral-storage-metrics" to ServiceAccount monitoring/k8s-ephemeral-storage-metrics

steps: Identify which subjects are bound to the nodes/proxy ClusterRole
Remove unnecessary bindings or switch to more restrictive ClusterRoles
Audit ServiceAccount usage to verify necessity
Restrict binding scope where possible
Related policy controls: KPOL-0279 and KPOL-0367
